title: Putharo
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (rice flour, water/coconut milk). Serve with vegetarian sides only for Jain-friendly meal.
recipe: Mix rice flour with water (or coconut milk) into a smooth batter of pouring consistency.
Pour into a traditional earthen pan (sarao) or steamer and cook till soft and spongy.
Serve hot with vegetarian sides like sesame dal, turmeric rice or red tea.
tips: Soft steamed rice flatbread – classic Khasi breakfast item.
Traditionally paired with pork curry, but can be enjoyed with vegetarian sides.

title: Pukhlein
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (rice flour, jaggery, oil).
recipe: Mix rice flour with melted jaggery and a little water into a thick dough.
Shape into small discs or balls and deep-fry till golden and crisp outside.
Serve as a sweet snack with tea.
tips: Popular Khasi fried rice cake – crispy exterior, chewy and mildly sweet inside.
Common street and tea-time snack.

title: Pumaloi
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (powdered rice, coconut, water, salt). Ensure coconut is fresh and pure.
recipe: Mix powdered rice with water (and grated coconut if using) into a smooth batter.
Steam in a traditional pot or steamer till cooked through and soft.
Serve warm as a light breakfast or side.
tips: Steamed powdered-rice cake – oil-free and nutritious.
A gentle, everyday Khasi breakfast item.

title: Jadoh
jainNotes: Contains pork - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Cook pork pieces with turmeric, ginger and salt till the fat renders and meat is tender.
Add washed rice and enough water. Cook together so the rice absorbs the pork juices and fat.
Serve hot, often with dohkhlieh, tungrymbai or a simple vegetable side.
tips: Signature Khasi one-pot rice-and-pork dish – the state's most iconic meal.
The rice should be richly flavoured and slightly oily from the pork.

title: Dohkhlieh
jainNotes: Contains pork and onion - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Boil pork till tender, then shred or finely chop while still warm.
Mix with finely sliced onion, green chilli, crushed ginger, salt and a squeeze of lime.
Serve at room temperature as a refreshing meat salad alongside jadoh or rice.
tips: Classic Khasi pork salad – light, pungent and herb-fresh.
A perfect counterpoint to richer rice dishes.

title: Tungrymbai (Vegetarian)
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Black sesame, ginger, garlic, onion, chilli

recipe: Sauté onion, ginger, garlic and chilli in oil.
Add the fermented soybeans and black sesame. Mix well and simmer till the flavours meld.
Serve as a strong-flavoured side with rice or jadoh.
tips: Fermented soybean dish with a powerful, earthy aroma – an acquired taste.
Vegetarian version of the traditional Khasi preparation.

title: Tungrymbai with Pork
jainNotes: Contains pork, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Black sesame, ginger, garlic, onion, chilli

recipe: Sauté onion, ginger, garlic and chilli. Add chopped pork and cook till done.
Add the fermented soybeans and black sesame. Mix well and simmer till the flavours meld.
Serve as a strong-flavoured side with rice or jadoh.
tips: Traditional Tungrymbai with pork - the classic Khasi preparation.
Fermented soybean dish with a powerful, earthy aroma.

title: Dohneiiong
jainNotes: Contains pork - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Dry-roast and grind black sesame seeds into a paste.
Cook pork with ginger, garlic and chilli till tender. Add the sesame paste and simmer till the gravy thickens and coats the meat.
Serve with rice.
tips: Pork in rich black sesame sauce – nutty, dark and deeply flavourful.
A Jaintia and Khasi favourite.

title: Nakham Bitchi
jainNotes: Contains dried fish, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Soak dried fish briefly. Make a spicy paste with chilli, ginger and garlic.
Cook the fish with the paste and a little water into a thick, fiery gravy or soup.
Serve with rice – a classic Garo preparation.
tips: Spicy dried-fish dish from Garo cuisine.
Intense flavour typical of smoked and dried ingredients used in the hills.

title: Ja Stem (Turmeric Rice)
recipe: Cook rice with turmeric and salt till fluffy and yellow.
Serve plain or with simple sides, pickles or as part of a light meal.
tips: Simple turmeric-coloured rice – a vegetarian option in Khasi homes.
Often eaten with sesame dal or vegetable sides.

title: Tungtap
jainNotes: Contains fermented/smoked fish, onion - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Pound or finely chop the fermented smoked fish with chilli, onion and ginger.
Mix into a strong, pungent chutney or relish.
Serve as a side with rice or any meal.
tips: Powerful fermented fish chutney – used sparingly for its intense flavour.
A classic Khasi condiment.

title: Dai Sboh (Black Sesame Dal)
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.
recipe: Cook lentils till soft. Roast and grind black sesame.
Sauté onion and garlic, then mix the sesame paste into the dal along with ginger and chilli. Simmer briefly.
Serve with rice or ja stem.
tips: Nutty black-sesame lentil preparation – a vegetarian Khasi favourite.
Pairs well with turmeric rice.

title: Wak Tangsek Pura
jainNotes: Contains pork - not consumed by Jains.
recipe: Cook pork with a little indigenous alkali/soda till tender.
Add chopped greens and powdered rice to thicken. Season and simmer.
Serve with rice – a traditional Garo pork-and-greens dish.
tips: Garo specialty using local alkali (from ash) for distinctive flavour and texture.
Hearty and rustic.
